claim: A set-account-mode flip made through scripts/ops/set_account_mode.sh is reverted in config/accounts.yaml within ~5 minutes by ict-git-sync, and reverts at runtime at the next trader restart, because the script edits only the VM working tree and never commits to main.
evidence: scripts/ops/set_account_mode.sh:125-148 edits ${REPO_DIR}/config/accounts.yaml in place (python p.write_text) and restarts ict-trader-live; `grep -n 'git commit\|git push' scripts/ops/set_account_mode.sh .github/workflows/system-actions.yml` -> no output. scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:116-117 `echo ">>> Hard-resetting to origin/main (VM is a read-only mirror)..."; git reset --hard origin/main`. deploy/ict-git-sync.service ExecStart=scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh; deploy/ict-git-sync.timer:13 `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`. Live read 2026-09-27 `curl https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/config` -> yaml_mode for all 11 accounts equals repo config/accounts.yaml (no flip currently in effect).
expected: An audited Tier-2 mode flip (the only sanctioned writer of `mode:`, docs/claude/system-actions.md §2.1) persists until reversed by the operator.
actual: The YAML edit is wiped by the next git-sync hard reset (<=5 min); the in-memory mode persists only until the next restart of ict-trader-live (any deploy), then silently returns to origin/main's value. /api/bot/config exposes only yaml_mode, so the interval where runtime != YAML is invisible.
population: 1 writer script (set_account_mode.sh) x 1 sync path (deploy_pull_restart.sh via ict-git-sync.timer); 11 accounts read live, 0 currently divergent.
detector: A test in tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py asserting that the set-account-mode path either commits the change to main or that deploy_pull_restart.sh preserves accounts.yaml mode; none exists today (grep tests/ for set_account_mode finds only the dispatch-map entry).
proposed_fix: Make the flip durable: have the set-account-mode workflow commit the one-line mode change to main (with the operator marker check_dry_run_in_diff.py already expects) before/after the VM edit, so git-sync converges on it instead of reverting it. Tier-2: operator OK required.

claim: scripts/ops/reconcile_orphan_history.py --apply can write the same order_package_id onto two trades in different accounts in one run, because _recover_package matches on symbol + direction + entry price only, with no position_size gate, no linked_trade_id check and no cross-cluster de-duplication.
evidence: scripts/ops/reconcile_orphan_history.py:182-218 SELECT ... FROM order_packages WHERE symbol=? ORDER BY datetime(created_at) DESC LIMIT 60, then returns first row with matching canonical direction and |entry-pe|/pe<=entry_tol. `grep -n 'position_size\|consumed' scripts/ops/reconcile_orphan_history.py` -> only line 169 (the trades SELECT). Live matcher: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:3905 _recover_orphan_attribution and :3992 _recover_orphan_order_package both reference position_size. Subagent repro on a scratch DB built with Database(): trades id=1 bybit_1 size 1.0 entry 50005, id=2 bybit_2 size 100.0 entry 50003, one package pkg-1 entry 50000 -> dry-run plans both rows `reconciled_to_package: 'pkg-1'`.
expected: One order package is attributed to at most one trade, with the same size gate the live matcher uses (docstring claims to be a 'mirror of order_monitor._recover_orphan_...').
actual: The package is handed to every cluster whose entry is within tolerance, regardless of account or size.
population: 1 function; 8 existing tests in tests/test_reconcile_orphan_history.py, none with more than one account or package (all pass).
detector: Add a test with two orphan trades in different accounts/sizes and one order package, asserting only one attribution; it fails on current code.
proposed_fix: Port order_monitor's position_size gate into _recover_package, skip packages with a non-null linked_trade_id belonging to another trade, and track attributed package ids across clusters in _plan_cluster/run, refusing a second attribution.

claim: 30 of 93 pipeline items in state `routed` name only checklist rows that are done or dropped, and because unrouted() excludes every `routed` item they are counted by nothing: brief §5's unrouted number (72) omits them.
evidence: python3 script over read_log(STORE) + MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json matching checklist ids in routed_to -> `93 Counter({'some named row open': 40, 'all named rows done/dropped': 30, 'no checklist id': 23})`; e.g. PI-20260921-E3-ORB-NO-SLIPPAGE routed_to 'E7' (E7 state done), PI-20260921-LANE-BLOCKED-ON-AN-UNATTENDED-PERMISSION-PROMPT routed_to 'E44 ...' (E44 dropped). scripts/ops/pipeline.py:669-676 unrouted() = due items with state != 'routed'.
expected: An item whose owner finished or was dropped returns to the unrouted count (pipeline.py docstring: 'A routing with no destination is how an item stops being anyone's').
actual: It stays `routed` forever; 25 of the 93 routed items are computed-due and still excluded.
population: 93 routed items of 1395 in docs/claude/work/pipeline (1708 records), 2026-09-27.
detector: A pipeline.py --check step that joins routed_to against MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and reports routed items whose every named owner row is done/dropped (count always printed, including 0).
proposed_fix: Treat routed items whose owner row is terminal as unrouted in unrouted(); add the join to --check and to brief §0.
disposition: open — not filed separately; recorded here for the manager to route

claim: 625 of 806 open pipeline items carry an origin.rerun that only prints the archived register row, so the command cannot tell whether the finding still applies — reason (3) of pipeline.py is met in form and not in substance.
evidence: python3 over read_log(STORE): `open 806 open w/ rerun reading docs/archive 625`; example BL-20260812-TRAINER-STRAY-REPO-ROOT-JOURNAL-DB rerun = `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/registers/health-review-backlog.json')); ... print(json.dumps(next(i for i in items if i.get('id')=='BL-...'), indent=2))"`. scripts/ops/pipeline.py:289-294 validates rerun only as a non-empty string.
expected: origin.rerun is 'the command that REGENERATES the finding, so a successor can ask whether it still applies' (pipeline.py docstring reason 3).
actual: For 78% of open items it re-reads a frozen archive; the validator cannot distinguish the two.
detector: --check could count (and print) open items whose rerun only reads docs/archive/; a hard refusal would block legitimate imports, so a reported count is the realistic detector.
proposed_fix: Report the count in --check and brief §5; triage imported rows (A8) by replacing the rerun with a real re-check or killing the row with a terminal_reason.

claim: CLAUDE.md § 'The follow-through pipeline' says the brief (A3) is not built, nothing runs render_section_0, and the store is seeded empty with A8 not run — the field contradicts all three.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:129-140 ('THE PULL IS BUILT BUT NOT YET CONNECTED... the brief that displays them is `A3` and is not built'; 'The store is seeded empty on purpose; importing them is `A8`'). Field: src/web/api/routers/work.py:2150-2188 GET /api/bot/work/brief calls render_daily_brief.build(), which calls pipeline.render_section_0 (render_daily_brief.py:209); live `curl https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/work/brief` 2026-09-27T13:29Z -> present true, '## §0 — WHAT CAME DUE ... 97 item(s) due', pipelineStats records 1708 / items 1395 / due 97 / unrouted 72 — identical to local `python3 scripts/ops/pipeline.py --check`. Checklist: A3 done, A7 done, A8 landed_unproven; store holds 561 open BL-* items imported by MIGR records.
expected: CLAUDE.md describes the pipeline's current wiring.
actual: It describes the pre-A3, pre-A8 state; render_section_0 IS called on every /brief request (observed live), though whether the SPA Workflow page displays /brief was not checked (other repo).
population: 3 claims in CLAUDE.md:129-140 vs code + 1 live read.
detector: canonical-doc-coherence could assert that CLAUDE.md does not say 'A3 ... is not built' while the checklist row A3 is done; no generic detector for prose staleness.
proposed_fix: Rewrite CLAUDE.md §'The follow-through pipeline' to: pull connected via GET /api/bot/work/brief (observed 2026-09-27); A8 imported the archived rows (landed_unproven).

claim: CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, the close-out/manager/health-review/performance-review skills and the .claude/settings.json session-start hook name docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl as the intake, but that file does not exist; the store is the directory docs/claude/work/pipeline/, and pipeline.py has no CLI command that files a record.
evidence: `ls docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl` -> No such file or directory; `ls docs/claude/work/pipeline | wc -l` -> 1708; scripts/ops/pipeline.py:186 STORE = Path('docs/claude/work/pipeline'). `grep -rln PIPELINE.jsonl CLAUDE.md docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md .claude/` -> CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, .claude/skills/{health-review,performance-review,close-out,manager}/SKILL.md, .claude/settings.json; 84 non-archive files in total. `python3 scripts/ops/pipeline.py --help` -> only --self-test --check --due --stats --mint-id --store (no append); --due is parsed but unused (main() renders §0 by default). render_daily_brief.py:37-39 docstring also still says 'docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl' and 'config/mandates.yaml (today: absent — B5 is not built)'.
expected: Instructions name the real store and a real filing command.
actual: A session following them either hand-writes PIPELINE.jsonl (which --check's _resurrected_legacy_file then fails, pipeline.py:1096-1132 — good) or has to discover append() in the source.
population: 84 files outside docs/archive and docs/audits naming PIPELINE.jsonl; 7 of them canonical instructions.
detector: A run_guards step failing when CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md or .claude/settings.json mention docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl.
proposed_fix: Replace the path in canonical docs/skills/hook with docs/claude/work/pipeline/; add `pipeline.py --file <json> --intent new|update` wrapping append() so the documented CLI works.

evidence: scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py:262-264 `L.append(f"- `{m.get('id','?')}` — {m.get('grants', m)}")`. config/mandates.yaml:367 MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 `blocked_until: >-`; :465 MD-DEMOTE-S2-S1 `autoland: true`. claim: scripts/ops/session_reaper.py reads the retired docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, and when it is missing prints 'unreadable 0' and exits 0 even with --strict.
evidence: `python3 scripts/ops/session_reaper.py --no-fetch --strict; echo exit=$?` -> '0 row(s) graded ... unreadable 0 ... exit=0'. --json shows registry_read_state 'unreadable: [Errno 2] No such file ...'. session_reaper.py:123 REGISTRY path; :449-455 catches and sets rows=[]; :677 --strict only checks per-row unreadable. .github/workflows/session-reaper.yml: cron commented out, but push paths still include docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json (dead) and scripts/ops/session_reaper.py, plus workflow_dispatch; invoked with --write and without --strict.
expected: A missing input registry is a hard failure, or at least is shown in default output.
actual: Green run, ledger written claiming 0 sessions graded.
population: 1 script, 1 workflow; registry absent at the read path (git ls-files).
detector: --strict should fail when registry_read_state != 'read'; test_session_reaper.py could add a missing-file case.
proposed_fix: Fail (exit 1) on an unreadable registry, or retire the script and workflow with the register (the reset retired SESSIONS.json).

claim: scripts/ops/uncarried_specs.py --self-test fails on main (exit 1) because 6 of its 7 WORK_REGISTERS carriers are retired paths, and its CI guard was removed, so nothing notices.
evidence: `python3 scripts/ops/uncarried_specs.py --self-test; echo $?` -> 'FAIL — POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: docs/design/operating-layer-build-plan-DESIGN.md graded 'mentioned'...' exit 1. uncarried_specs.py:123-131 WORK_REGISTERS = work/objects, work/intents, work/steps, OPEN-ITEMS.json, MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, DUE.json, WORK-DIGEST.json. scripts/ci/run_guards.py:200 '# Removed: ... uncarried-spec-guard ...'.
